The newly debuted Juiced Scrambler Mini looks like it could do a pretty good job of threading that needle.

The newly introduced youth-sized e-bike takes the mini-motorcycle styling of Juiced’s larger Scrambler models and shrinks it down around 16-inch fat tires, creating a bike designed for riders between 4’0″ and 5’3″ (122 to 160 cm). But perhaps more importantly for parents, Juiced also built in a PIN-protected speed limiter known as Speed Lock that lets adults decide just how fast the bike can go.

The Scrambler Mini ships set to a 10 mph (16 km/h) Beginner Mode, but its maximum speed can be adjusted anywhere from 1-20 mph (32 km/h) and then locked behind a four-digit PIN. Juiced notes that riders aged 8-12 should not exceed 10 mph, while riders 13 and older can use the bike at speeds up to 20 mph, subject of course to local laws and regulations. In almost every state and jurisdiction though, the bike will fit Class 2 designation for street-legal riding and bike lane operation.

That setup seems like a pretty smart way to approach youth e-bikes. Instead of buying a slow bike that a teenager may quickly outgrow – or handing them a much faster machine before a parent thinks they’re ready – the same bike can essentially grow with the rider (with speed titrated by a parent or guardian).

And from the kid’s perspective, it certainly doesn’t look like a safety-first children’s bike.

The Scrambler Mini gets the same sort of moto-inspired styling that has defined Juiced’s Scrambler lineup, including a long bench seat, dual-crown-style fork, chunky 16 x 4-inch tires, and several appropriately loud color options including Blackberry, Fruit Punch, Blueberry, and Pink Lemonade.

Industry observers note that there’s some decent hardware underneath that styling, too. The rear hub motor is rated at 500W nominal and 1,092W peak with 80 Nm of torque. A removable 48V 10Ah battery using LG cells provides 480Wh of capacity, with Juiced claiming up to 40 miles (64 km) of range. Four levels of cadence-based pedal assist are included, as is a right-side thumb throttle.

The bike also features Talon hydraulic disc brakes with large 180mm rotors front and rear, 50mm of front suspension travel, an integrated backlit LCD, a headlight, and a rear taillight with brake-light functionality. The single-speed bike weighs 59 lb (26.8 kg), has a 27.15-inch seat height, and is rated for up to 275 lb (125 kg) of payload.

Those parts are far above what we normally see on e-bikes targeted towards teens, with most teen-focused e-bikes sporting cheaper components like mechanical brakes and rigid forks.

The Scrambler Mini is listed at $1,099, though Juiced is presently offering a Black Friday sale that drops the price by another $150 to just $949. The company indicates preorders are expected to begin shipping the week of December 7.

Industry observers note that that price also comes with something increasingly important in the crowded youth e-bike market: an actual company standing behind the bike. Juiced was founded in 2009, quickly becoming a leader in the market for powerful and stylish e-bikes. But after the brand’s financial troubles a few years ago, Lectric eBikes stepped in to take Juiced under its wing in 2025. The relaunched Juiced now offers a three-year manufacturer warranty and US-based support, plus the peace of mind that comes with backing from North America’s largest e-bike company, Lectric eBikes.

That last part may be just as appealing to parents as the speed limiter, though the 3-year warranty is definitely a deal sweetener, too.

There’s always going to be some controversy around the idea of e-bikes marketed towards teens, but I’m for it when done responsibly. Let’s face it: e-bikes are incredibly popular and teens are already going to be riding them, even if it means borrowing a friend’s e-bike because they don’t have their own. So if they’re going to be riding, the least we can do is put them on a safer, higher-quality bike so they learn the right skills in the right environment. And hey, it sure beats teens sitting alone in their rooms texting each other all afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to choosing an e-bike, there are already plenty of cheap mini e-bikes and electric dirt bike-style machines floating around online, and many are undoubtedly going to look tempting to teenagers. The Scrambler Mini seems to take a different approach, giving young riders the styling, fat tires, throttle, and mini-moto attitude they actually want, while giving parents control over how much of that performance they can access.

It’s still an e-bike capable of 20 mph, and that means parents need to make decisions about where, when, and how their kids ride it. And there’s even an argument to be made for removing the throttle and turning it into a Class 1 e-bike in the beginning, requiring a teen to pedal it to engage the motor. But I’d much rather see that conversation happening around a bike with hydraulic brakes, lights, a programmable speed limit, and a real manufacturer standing behind it than around some anonymous electric mini-bike bought from the depths of the internet.

And if the teenager thinks it looks cool enough to actually ride, that’s probably the point.

Mathematicians make a breakthrough in 174-year-old problem

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that while mathematicians technically solved a nearly 175-year-old theorem known as the Four-Color Problem in 1976, the problem continues to vex researchers.
  • The underlying conceit to the Four-Color Problem is deceptively straightforward.
  • It took more than 85 years until a full proof arrived—a particularly notable moment, since it was also the first major theorem proven by a computer program.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that while mathematicians technically solved a nearly 175-year-old theorem known as the Four-Color Problem in 1976, the problem continues to vex researchers. For some in the field, their fascination with the perniciously complex concept runs so deep, that they liken their obsession to a lingering disease. But after a decade of analysis, an international team of mathematicians has made the first major breakthrough in the ongoing Four-Color Problem saga in 30 years. At this year’s Foundations of Computer Science (FOCS) conference, investigators laid out the optimal, most efficient algorithm that solves the Four-Color Problem.

The underlying conceit to the Four-Color Problem is deceptively straightforward. In 1852, 19th century English mathematician Francis Guthrie posited that you only need a quartet of hues to fill every border-enclosed region on a map. Think all territories, regions, states, and nations filled in with only four colors. The first proof was introduced in 1879, and seemed solid for 11 years. That is, until Guthrie’s colleagues found an error in the calculations.

It took more than 85 years until a full proof arrived—a particularly notable moment, since it was also the first major theorem proven by a computer program. However, many in the mathematical community took concern with the digital discovery after having difficulty verifying it themselves.

It has been revealed that A more accessible proof arrived in 1997, but even then, the algorithmic system became painfully slow as sample maps grew larger. A handful of mathematicians around the world have pondered new approaches to the problem ever since—including University of Copenhagen computer scientist Mikkel Thorup, who likens his interest to a “four-color disease.”.

Industry observers note that “I would guess that at least 1,000 mathematicians have caught the four-color disease, spending months trying to make it work but never quite succeeding,” Thorup stated in a university profile. “It is the disease people have suffered from since 1852.”.

According to recent reports, it took years, but Thorup and his colleagues made progress after uncovering a novel detail regarding map-like surfaces known as planar graphs. The researchers realized these graphs feature many more reducible arrangements than experts previously assumed. This provided them a much more discreet set of starting points.

According to recent reports, “Think of reducible configurations as handles you can grab hold on to start four-coloring,” added study co-author and Technical University of Denmark (DTU) mathematician Carsten Thomassen. “We show that graphs do not contain just one handle, but an astonishing number of them. Nobody knew that before.”.

Recent findings suggest that instead of one or two handles in a graph, the team could now identify many more handles throughout any given map. This allowed them to simultaneously begin filling regions with four colors, which exponentially quickened the overall process. Thomassen mentioned this boosted their algorithm from quadratic time (where calculation speed increases proportionally to the square of an input size) to linear time.

“This means that if a map contains ten times as many regions, the computation only becomes about ten times slower. With the previous algorithm, it would have become about 100 times slower,” he added.

In a recent development, but does this really change anything beyond theoretical mathematics? According to researchers, the answer is a resounding “yes.”.

“The remarkable thing is that because there are so many handles, the idea can also be applied to other kinds of surfaces besides a flat map,” stated Thorup. “For example, surfaces with holes, such as a swim ring or a piece of…cheese.”.

In a recent development, okay, so the implications may be somewhat subtle for most people’s day-to-day lives. That doesn’t change the fact that mathematicians finally worked through symptoms of their disease for the first time in 30 years. As to why Thorup and his colleagues spent a decade on a theorem whose major immediate implications are “cheese,” he had a relatively succinct explanation.

“Because mathematicians are slightly crazy. Most of what mathematicians work on consists of very nerdy questions,” he mentioned. “We become obsessed with this type of problem because it challenges the human intellect. And if we find the answer, we’ll probably also find answers to other mathematical puzzles.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • In a recent development, the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the newly introduced power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

In a recent development, the folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

According to recent reports, 10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini notes the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

The Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this latest architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

Sources indicate that the increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” says Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a fresh calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

It has been revealed that combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

Recent findings suggest that production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been announced, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

Latest Update: Is Your Obsession Actually Limerence?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (691 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • The experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least.
  • Are you someone who obsesses about others?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

The experience and expression of human attachment is complex, to say the least. As humans, we may share a universal ingrained wiring for connection, but how we navigate this interpersonal world is not the same from person to person.

Are you someone who obsesses about others? Maybe you understand infatuation in the early stages of love, but then know how to transition to a mutual relationship or let go? Forming steady and stable connections is easy for some people; others are tortured with intense and uncertain attachments. Upcoming research provides insight into limerence, a specific form of intense attachment that is starting to gain more attention.

Sources indicate that imagine someone fixating on another person. This isn't hard to do. We hear about it on podcasts, watch it unfold in fantastic crime dramas, and, of course, some of us experience it in real life. From infatuation to unrequited love, examples of preoccupations with another person, outside of established relationships, color the romantic landscape. Limerence, however, is different.

Recent findings suggest that limerence is an intense and highly disruptive cognitive and emotional experience (Marshall et al., 2025; Tennov, 1979). Individuals in the throes of limerence are overwhelmed by the desire to be viewed positively by a specific someone else (i.e., the limerence object). This obsession manifests as uncontrollable rumination to the point that it interferes with day-to-day life.

According to recent reports, limerence is typically expressed toward someone with whom the experiencer is highly unlikely to form a real relationship. On the surface, this might seem like unrequited love, but it is far more intense and generally less realistic.

From a case study analysis, Wyant (2021) offered the following pathway by which people might come to experience limerence:.

It has been revealed that A recent review (Bradbury et al., 2025) summarized a step-wise sequence proposed by Verhulst (1984). This model suggests that limerence begins in the context of need: a person's needs for emotional intimacy, support, and connection are not fulfilled in their current relationships. Limerence can follow from there:.

Recent findings suggest that different dimensions of limerence are predictable by key psychological constructs. Recent research suggests limerence is best understood as a two-dimensional construct, comprised of both an intense need for attachment and neglect of self or others (Marshall et al., 2025).

According to recent reports, attachment anxiety, imaginative fantasy (i.e., the tendency to daydream), and the need to belong are linked to the need-for-attachment dimension of limerence for those experiencing it. This dimension is also predicted by psychological inflexibility and emotional dependence, obsessive preoccupation, self-conscious anxiety, and idealization (Marshall et al., 2025). The neglect dimension operates similarly, except it is not predicted by attachment orientation or idealization, and is associated with more social anxiety and lower self-esteem.

In a recent development, whereas scholars have noted parallels between limerence and addiction and noted the potential path from limerence to stalking (e.g., Bradbury et al., 2025), there's reason to suggest that limerence can also serve as a coping mechanism in an unfulfilling relational context. Experiencing limerence can be a one-time experience or repeated, short-lived or long (Tennov, 1979), yet the context in which it occurs offers the suggestion that it is the mind's way of addressing an undermet need for belonging and intimacy. The field has much more to learn about limerence as an unusual manifestation of the human attachment system.

According to recent reports, bradbury, P., Short, E., & Bleakley, P. (2025). Limerence, hidden obsession, fixation, and rumination: A scoping review of human behaviour. Journal of Police and Criminal Psychology, 40(2), 417-426.

The Toyota bZ Woodland comes standard with a dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain, delivering a combined 375 horsepower, which is 37 hp more than the standard bZ SUV with AWD.

According to recent reports, toyota’s standard bZ is offered with FWD and AWD powertrains. FWD models deliver either 165 hp (XLE FWD) or 221 hp (XLE FWD Plus and Limited FWD), while AWD models produce a combined 338 hp.

The Woodland model is also 6″ longer than the standard bZ, opening up an additional 30 cubic feet of cargo space on the inside.

Toyota’s bigger SUV also adds a rugged look and off-road capabilities with 8.3″ of ground clearance and up to 3,500 lbs of towing capacity.

Other rugged upgrades are standard, including All-Terrain tires, black side molding, roof rails, and black wheel arch cladding.

Inside, both come with a 7″ digital cluster and a large 14″ touchscreen running the latest Toyota Audio Multimedia system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

Although it uses the same 74.7-kWh battery as the standard bZ, the Woodland version offers slightly less driving range because of the added power and off-road equipment. The 2027 bZ Woodland has an estimated range of up to 281 miles with all-season tires, or 260 miles with the optional all-terrain tires.

Sources indicate that in comparison, the bZ is available with two battery packs: 57.7 kWh and 74.7 kWh. The base XLE FWD uses the 57.7 kWh battery, while the XLE AWD and FWD Plus, Limited AWD, and FWD models use the 74.7 kWh battery.

The standard 57.7 kWh battery provides an EPA range of up to 236 miles, while the 74.7 kWh battery provides up to 314 miles for FWD and 288 miles for AWD.

Recent findings suggest that both the bZ and bZ Woodland have a native NACS port, so drivers can use Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter. It takes around 30 minutes to charge the battery from 10% to 80%.

The 2027 Toyota bZ Woodland is available in Base and Premium trims, starting at $45,380, or over $10,000 more than the standard bZ.

Melissa Joan Hart Explains It All: Hot Flashes, Menopause, and Turning 50

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (949 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off.
  • Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline.
  • Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Actor Melissa Joan Hart has a vivid memory of her mother standing in front of their open freezer to cool off. As a child, she didn’t understand why. Now, as a 50-year-old woman, Hart knows that her mom was experiencing hot flashes.

Recent findings suggest that “[She’s] only 20 years older than me, so maybe I missed the part where she was going through [menopause], but there was no conversation about it,” Hart told Healthline. “I feel like it’s just becoming a hot topic with women, where…the taboo is going away from it now.”.

Her own perimenopausal symptoms started with night sweats.

“[It] was really jarring, and the first few times, you’re not really sure what that was…do I need to turn the air down or what’s going on here?” Hart stated.

Over time, she learned that she was experiencing moderate to severe hot flashes, which affect up to 80% of women during the menopause transition and can persist for 7 to 10 years.

Doctors categorize hot flashes as mild, moderate, or severe, stated Diana Bitner, MD, OB-GYN, at Corewell Health.

Recent findings suggest that “[So] if they’re mild, it’s a sense of warmth (maybe in the chest, or the neck, or the face). A moderate hot flash is where there’s associated sweating, and a severe hot flash is something that stops you in your tracks, wakes you up from the middle of the night,” Bitner told Healthline.

Sources indicate that hart has mostly experienced hot flashes while home or at her three sons’ activities, and they have yet to interfere with her work. However, according to research, one in three women report moderate to severe challenges in managing their work due to symptoms related to menopause.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s just so sad that about 10% of women leave the workforce due to menopause,” said Bitner. “And so it can really affect our ability to perform at these key years of not only institutional memory, but also of earning power, and it can really affect the whole community.”.

Bitner said women should feel empowered to bring up their menopausal symptoms or questions with their doctor.

“[This] is something that was taboo for so long…women didn’t really talk about this, whether it was because of embarrassment, or [they] weren’t sure if anyone was experiencing it,” she remarked. “[There’s] no reason, in this day and age, we need to suffer through it…it’s something that there are treatment options for.”.

In fact, Bitner stated providing specific details about their symptoms, such as how many mild, moderate, or severe hot flashes they’ve experienced over the past week, can help doctors better assess patients’ needs.

Hart looks to discuss treatment options for her hot flashes with her doctor soon. In the last few years, she mentioned she has put emphasis on her midlife health.

“I just was sick of waking up with aches and pains in general [thinking], ‘is this the rest of my life?’” she mentioned.

She started listening to self-help books in the car while driving her kids around and found ways to put herself first.

“My kids are a little bit older, so I kind of have that freedom to be able to do that,” she remarked. “[But] along with getting older, comes the menopause, comes that different time in life. And I think it’s a good time to reevaluate [how] our bodies can’t handle what [they] used to handle, and let’s figure it out.”.

Hart has partnered with pharmaceutical manufacturer Bayer on its “Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash” campaign, which encourages women to discuss menopause symptoms with their doctors and promotes Lynkuet, a hormone-free prescription medication for moderate to severe hot flashes associated with menopause.

It has been revealed that “It’s called ‘Life Doesn’t Stop for a Hot Flash’ campaign because it shouldn’t, because we should be able to push through, and this should be a time in our lives when our kids are getting older, and we’re able to kind of reinvent ourselves,” mentioned Hart. “And I think it’s an exciting time, and it shouldn’t be something that we’re afraid of.”.

She is embracing speaking openly about midlife health.

“I hit 50 this year, and it was, like, a huge milestone, and I think that’s something to be proud of, and not something to shy away from,” she remarked.

Hart also hopes to challenge the longstanding barriers women face in Hollywood as they age, including fewer opportunities for leading roles.

“[I] think we’re seeing that the generation before, and my generation, it feels like we’re pushing those boundaries…and we’re saying, you know, that women at this age have a lot to give, have a lot of information to share, have a lot of stories to tell and experiences and adventures still ahead of us, and, you know, we’re not ready to stop,” Hart said.

In everyday life, Bitner mentioned that while some patients avoid talking about midlife issues like menopause with their doctors, she is seeing more patients who are confident being forthcoming.

Industry observers note that as more women talk openly about menopause, she hopes to include men in the conversation, too. In fact, she invites her patients to bring their partners to appointments, so they can gain an understanding of menopause and the experiences their partners face, such as hot flashes, sleep problems, vaginal dryness, and discomfort or pain during intercourse.

It has been revealed that “[Often], there’s, you know, comments that come up [from men who] say, ‘How do I talk about this without getting in trouble?’” mentioned Bitner. “[We] want everyone to join this conversation…it doesn’t have to be just her problem because we know it’s not.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nesting season has officially begun for the seabirds visiting Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge near Hawaii.
  • Black-footed albatrosses are typically the first to lay eggs beginning in November.
  • According to recent reports, one special albatross couple has already been spotted—George and Geraldine.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nesting season has officially begun for the seabirds visiting Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge near Hawaii. The first egg of the season was laid by a black-footed albatross (Phoebastria nigripes) or kaʻupu in Hawaiian. Field biologist and photographer Dan Rapp captured video of this exciting first, which Friends of Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge shared on social media.

Black-footed albatrosses are typically the first to lay eggs beginning in November. The Laysan albatross (Phoebastria immutabilis) or mōlī in Hawaiian, will lay their eggs in late November through December. Every fall, this remote group of islands about 1,250 miles from Honolulu temporarily becomes the world’s largest albatross colony. Albatrosses are a group of large migratory seabird species, and includes the wandering albatross (Diomedea exulans), which has the largest wingspan of any living bird species.

According to recent reports, one special albatross couple has already been spotted—George and Geraldine. The duo is together for the 10th straight year. George was first spotted exactly one month ago on October 18, and the couple was reunited by October 22. The pair are short-tailed albatrosses (Phoebastria albatrus) or makalena in Hawaiian. Short-tailed albatrosses can live up to 50 years and are monogamous—clearly.

According to recent reports, wisdom, a particularly famous bird in these parts, has not been spotted just yet. The over 70-year-old Laysan albatross is the oldest known banded wild bird in the world. She was first identified and banded in 1956 by wildlife biologist Chandler Robbins after she laid a single egg. Biologists estimate that she has produced 50 to 60 eggs and as many as 30 of her chicks have fledged in her lifetime. In 2024, Wisdom became the world’s oldest known wild bird to successfully lay an egg at the estimated age of 74. In March, she became a grandmother again.

Viewers can take in the sights and sounds of the albatross colony via live cameras and follow Friends of Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge for updates.

Viewers can expect to see the birds return to the islands, perform various courtship dances, begin to nest, lay their eggs, and eventually watch albatross chicks in all their fluffy glory.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • We’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The revision, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

We’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The enhancement kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

Industry observers note that there’s a fresh limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other substantial new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

In a recent development, these are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

In a recent development, the fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a substantial overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this revision, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several concerns that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.

Scout Motors starts validation builds at $2B SC plant, deliveries in 2028

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • According to recent reports, according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

According to recent reports, according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

It has been revealed that the Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout states more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

Fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The organization says the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Industry observers note that when Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout remarked it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

It has been revealed that it might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

The product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout debuted as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original blueprint, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

In a recent development, for comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

Sources indicate that A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a big number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

Industry observers note that but validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where new automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

September 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

According to recent reports, and the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

Sources indicate that but by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all strategy to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

According to recent reports, we’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

South Korea will use emergency alert system to warn about exam cheaters

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that on Thursday morning, millions of phones across South Korea will belt out a loud, buzzing alert normally intended to warn residents about earthquakes or other disasters.
  • Officials plan to send the notifications ahead of Suneung, the country’s notoriously gruelling, eight-hour-long college entrance exam, in an attempt to flush out any of the roughly 550,000 test-takers who may have smuggled in a banned smartphone.
  • The aggressive, last-minute measures come just days after a student in a national tax accountant exam admitted he used a miniature camera and a generative AI tool to achieve a near-perfect score.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that on Thursday morning, millions of phones across South Korea will belt out a loud, buzzing alert normally intended to warn residents about earthquakes or other disasters. This time, the alert is targeting a much different kind of public threat: sneaky standardized test cheaters.

Officials plan to send the notifications ahead of Suneung, the country’s notoriously gruelling, eight-hour-long college entrance exam, in an attempt to flush out any of the roughly 550,000 test-takers who may have smuggled in a banned smartphone. Proctors will also inspect all pairs of glasses for hidden cameras, and students wearing clothes with buttons will have to cover them with stickers.

The aggressive, last-minute measures come just days after a student in a national tax accountant exam admitted he used a miniature camera and a generative AI tool to achieve a near-perfect score. That surprise revelation sent educators and officials scrambling to come up with solutions to instill confidence in the upcoming test.

Sources indicate that korea’s measures come as educators around the world are struggling to keep up with a growing arsenal of AI-enabled tools that make cheating easier than ever. But while AI is the focus today, students have been tinkering with fresh tech and other creative ways to skirt the rules for as long as tests have carried weight.

Sources indicate that the sudden rule changes in South Korea come days after a 34-year-old man named Han Won-seok posted a video on his lawyer’s YouTube channel admitting he used AI to cheat on the country’s national tax exam. According to the Associated Press, Han scored 397.5 out of 400 points on the first stage of the multiple-choice test, a suspicious result that made him the subject of several media interviews. Other test-takers saw those results and accused him of trickery.

Days after denying those allegations, Han reversed course. In the video, he admitted to using a miniature camera to photograph the exam questions, which were then fed to an AI tool. He then viewed the AI-generated answers on his smartphone. Now, Han states he is cooperating with investigators and is warning others against following his lead.

“I cheated on the tax accountant exam. I sincerely apologize for causing damage to a lot of people,” the student said in the video, according to CNN. “If there is someone thinking of cheating like I did, I’m going to tell the investigators everything, so I hope you don’t think that you won’t get caught.”.

Industry observers note that in the days since the videos, officials have rushed to put in place latest anti-cheating safeguards. South Korean Prime Minister Han Sung-sook reportedly held a meeting on Monday with the country’s top education officials, where they agreed to officially add smart glasses to the list of prohibited items in testing rooms. Some lawmakers had reportedly even called on officials to postpone the Suneung exam until they could come up with more rigorous anti-cheating safeguards, though the country’s Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin quickly shot that idea down, arguing delays would cause “even a larger disruption.” And while Han never said he specifically used smart glasses to cheat, worries about that tech in particular aren’t hypothetical. Earlier this year, two other South Korean students taking an exam to assess English skills were also caught using camera-equipped glasses.

Concerns about AI-enabled cheating aren’t limited to South Korea either. Last week, England’s Office for Students, an independent higher education regulator, released a statement warning that AI tools are making it “close to impossible” to assess university classwork. In China, major tech companies disabled features on their AI apps during last year’s national college entrance exam (the gaokao), to keep students from using them to cheat. Educators in the United States and elsewhere are also increasingly requiring students to take exams in person and defend papers orally due to the pervasiveness of AI-generated submissions. Sales of Blue Books have soared as a result.

Industry observers note that while fancy AI tools and camera-equipped smart glasses may be new concerns, creative cheating isn’t. In fact, evidence of sneaky test-takers dates back centuries. One example is this replica of a linen vest from China’s Qing dynasty (1644–1911). The impressive garment has 62 essays, more than 40,000 characters in all, hidden inside. Students wearing the vest would sneak peeks during the country’s grueling imperial exams, which played an important role in determining government employment and social status. An even older Ming Dynasty (1368 to 1644) jacket was covered with some 50,000 characters from classical texts likely served a similar purpose.

Creative cheating has of course persisted into the modern era. In 2015, police in India’s Bihar state detained more than 1,000 people after relatives of test-takers were photographed scaling the walls of an exam center to pass cheat sheets to students through a window opening. A college student in the U.S. made headlines in 2011, after he was arrested for allegedly using fake IDs to stand in for at least six high school students during SAT exams. In China, a team of exam proctors equipped with  surveillance drones regularly seizes a variety of wearables and other devices students use to try and cheat. Among the seized items were a hidden camera placed inside a pen and glasses with cameras connected to a tiny receiver embedded in a coin.

One has to wonder if all that time and effort spent devising intricate cheating methods could have been used to study instead.

  • It has been revealed that hyundai debuted its latest liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable.
  • Industry observers note that the electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that genesis just added a newly introduced member to its growing family. the 2028 Genesis G80 Hybrid. It’s Genesis’s second-ever hybrid, to be precise—and the G80 Hybrid, along with the related GV80 Hybrid, will showcase the first Hyundai Motor Group (HMG) hybrid system with a liquid-cooled battery.

It has been revealed that hyundai debuted its latest liquid-cooled hybrid battery at a preview event on Tuesday, November 17, in Los Angeles, offering the media the chance to understand what makes it notable. By outperforming air-cooled systems with regard to temperature management, it unlocks higher peak discharge output and taps into more of the battery’s available power. Genesis first revealed its next-generation 2.5 Turbo Hybrid System for the GV80 Hybrid a few months ago, and now, we’re getting more details about how the same system will perform under the hood of the G80 Hybrid.

Industry observers note that the electric-assisted 2.5-liter turbocharged inline-four produces a hearty 347 horsepower—16 percent more than the standard four-cylinder G80 model—and 391 pound-feet of torque. The engine will be mated to a seven-speed automatic transmission, with a choice of “manual” or “smart” adjustable regenerative braking settings; the smart setting will automatically adjust regenerative braking levels based on navigation information and traffic conditions. The G80 Hybrid will come in rear-wheel drive.

Genesis claims the G80 Hybrid will feature 30-percent improved fuel economy over a comparable G80 model with 19-inch wheels, with driving range estimates extending to over 500 miles. Since these claims are based on internal testing, we’ll have to wait to see what final EPA fuel economy and driving range estimates are.

Want to be able to spot a G80 Hybrid in the wild? There are a few small changes to the exterior that should help you spot one. There’s a redesigned 3-D grille, new 18- and 20-inch wheel designs, and a range of new exterior colors; you can choose from Wadden Gray, Milos Blue, and Barolo Red. If you want to stand out from other G80 Hybrid models, a Prestige Black variant will be available with a blacked-out exterior and interior, plus exclusive Black Ash Wood and alloy wheels.

Sources indicate that inside, the G80 Hybrid is identical to the standard G80, with Nappa leather seating surfaces and distinct quilting patterns on different trim levels. You’ll also find the Genesis-familiar 27-inch OLED integrated instrument cluster and navigation display, as well as the comprehensive suite of advanced driver assistance technologies the brand bakes into its fresh models.

Genesis has yet to announce pricing details or a production date for the 2028 G80 Hybrid, but it seems likely they’ll start to reach dealers sometime in late 2027. Interested in seeing the Genesis G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid yourself before then? It will be displayed at the 2026 LA Auto Show during its public days, which run from November 20–29.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.
  • Ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron.
  • As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, consumers are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Social media influencers claim that having a “ferritin face” may indicate you’re low in iron.

Ferritin is a protein that helps your body store iron. You need iron in order to make healthy red blood cells, which carry oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body. Iron is also key for bone marrow, organs, healthy muscles, and brain development.

As “ferritin face” makes its way across social media platforms, consumers are describing several tell-tale signs, including:.

Customers have also shared images of their face before and after taking iron supplements or getting an iron infusion. Videos about “ferritin face” have garnered millions of views on various platforms.

However, medical professionals state that your appearance alone is not enough to diagnose iron deficiency.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s key to understand that ferritin face is not a medical diagnosis, nor is it a confirmed symptom of iron deficiency. While some people with iron deficiency can appear pale due to low hemoglobin levels in their red blood cells, there are many other symptoms to consider,” said Daniel Atkinson, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and clinical lead at Treated.

It has been revealed that “Notably, these symptoms are also present in many different conditions, and their presence does not necessarily mean iron deficiency anemia or even low ferritin levels. Similar features are seen in people with iron processing and absorption problems, such as gluten intolerance, or in urgent sudden blood loss scenarios,” added Jonathan Jennings, MD, board certified internist at Medical Offices of Manhattan.

Iron deficiency can affect your skin and appearance. These signs are often subtle, but may include:.

Sources indicate that in some ways, the social media videos are correct. Your skin and face can change when your iron levels are low.

“The facial signs people point to, like pale skin and a washed-out look, mostly come from anaemia, when your haemoglobin has dropped. But iron deficiency and anaemia aren’t the same thing,” said Thom Phillips, a general practitioner in the United Kingdom and Chief Medical Officer at Forth. “By the time low iron highlights on your face, your stores are usually close to empty.”.

It is notable to speak with a healthcare professional, who will run blood tests such as a complete blood count and ferritin levels.

It is also notable not to take iron supplements without first checking with your healthcare professional, because having too much iron in your body can also cause negative effects.

Too little and too much iron could raise your risk of infection, which is why it’s important not to take supplements without medical supervision.

Industry observers note that the signs and symptoms of iron deficiency can depend on whether you are anemic or not. Some of the early signs may include:.

“These symptoms typically occur because your body produces fewer red blood cells, which results in less oxygen being delivered throughout your body, making you feel tired and weak,” said Atkinson.

Less common symptoms may include:.

While your facial appearance can be a sign that something isn’t right, healthcare professionals consider other symptoms and how you feel overall.

They also rely on blood tests to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

“The misinformation is the idea that you can spot it yourself. That leads to two problems: people with low iron who look fine assume they’re OK, and people who look tired start taking iron supplements they don’t need,” remarked Phillips.

Atkinson also noted that factors such as different settings and environmental conditions can affect how your face appears.

That being said, the “ferritin face” trend may help bring awareness to certain symptoms and when to get them checked.

“[This] trend may raise some awareness about iron deficiency anemia and how low iron levels can impact daily life,” noted Atkinson.

Sources indicate that “Fatigue and lightheadedness are common side effects of low iron, but it manifests in other ways too, such as paler skin or increased hair shedding, which can be concerning for many people. If you experience these symptoms, you should let your doctor know so they can help treat the condition appropriately,” he said.

This Organization Wants to Import New Tiny Toyota Trucks from Thailand

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, here’s a new and unexpected sentence: A Thai tech giant wants to import small Japanese pickup trucks to the United States.
  • In a recent development, the base vehicle is a Toyota Hilux Champ.
  • Recent findings suggest that rok Trucks, a Thai upfitter that already deals in Hilux Champs, claims it will bring the little pickups here with the necessary changes to make them street legal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, here’s a new and unexpected sentence: A Thai tech giant wants to import small Japanese pickup trucks to the United States. It seems like the cheap-truck trend—see Slate’s Blank Slate, the Ford Maverick, and the upcoming Ford Fathom EV—caught the attention of some folks already dealing in little Toyotas, and now Rok Trucks has the U.S. market in its sights.

In a recent development, the base vehicle is a Toyota Hilux Champ. It does not fall under Japan’s kei minicar classification; the Hilux Champ is bigger, and it’s powered by four-cylinder gas and diesel engines. This is a smaller truck than Toyota’s Hilux, a favorite of insurgents and NGOs alike. It wasn’t designed for and is not legal on American streets—at least not yet.

See all results for used cars for sale near 16504.

Recent findings suggest that rok Trucks, a Thai upfitter that already deals in Hilux Champs, claims it will bring the little pickups here with the necessary changes to make them street legal. It already has approval in the United Kingdom, and the organization notes deliveries will begin there and in Ireland in early 2027. Canada, Australia, and Fresh Zealand are also on the to-do list.

The timing is more than a bit curious. Just last week, Toyota confirmed that it will assemble Daihatsu Hijet Jumbo kei trucks in Indiana and market them as the Scion by Toyota KEI-01. That baby pickup will be sold for fleet use only, at least at first, and it will be classified as a low-speed vehicle, keeping it to a top speed of 25 mph and to roads with speed limits of 35 mph or less. Rok Trucks states it isn’t going the LSV route and will instead sell a highway-ready pickup here.

Recent findings suggest that pricing is projected to start at $24,950, just under that $25K psychological barrier, inclusive of destination fees. The pickup version of the truck is available with three bed lengths, each named by its approximate measurement in millimeters—the BRT-1800 has a six-foot-two-inch bed; the BRT-2300’s bed measures seven feet, seven inches; and the BRT-2600’s bed is a healthy eight feet, eight inches. All beds are tray-style, with drop-down sides and a floor free from wheel well cutouts. The trucks have a 2200-pound payload rating.

Industry observers note that frills are few but include standard air conditioning and (it feels odd to have to mention this) power windows. A five-speed manual will be standard on the Base Rok, as will rear-wheel drive, with an automatic and four-wheel drive available. Necessary safety systems, such as airbags, automated emergency braking, and a rearview camera, are included as well. Paint colors appear limited to white, metallic silver, and metallic gray, while an optional wrap removes that constraint. We’ll guess that only gas engines will be offered in the States.

See all results for used cars for sale near 16504.

The manufacturer is taking reservations already, with $50 reserving a spot in line for a Classic Edition truck; for $999, buyers get one of 500 Founders Edition trucks, which puts them at the front of the production queue and includes several exclusive perks, such as priority support and a free color wrap for the truck’s cab. All reservations are refundable until you sign a purchase agreement.

Rok Trucks told The Autopian that it’s opening reservations now, before the truck has received regulatory approval, to gauge which of its many versions to bring to each market first. The Rok Trucks site shows 10 different upfits possible on top of the Base Rok. Some are pretty niche, like the Pet Rok, which is outfitted as a mobile dog spa. There are also box-van-like delivery trucks, a camper, the Rok Tipper with a dump bed, and the Baby G-Rok, which, as its name suggests, looks like a cross between a Mercedes G-wagen and a Casio G-Shock watch. The company also told The Autopian that Hilux Champs imported to the U.S. will wear Rok badging instead of Toyota branding.

Let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves, because many questions remain. It is neither cheap nor easy to make a vehicle that wasn’t originally designed for the U.S. market meet FMVSS and EPA regulations. Things like lighting locations and colors would likely have to be adjusted for conformity, and modifications to the vehicle structure may be required to pass crash tests. Also, crash testing is expensive.

Rok Trucks acknowledges that its product will be subject to the Chicken Tax, an old-school tariff of 25 percent that applies to imported vehicles, if the trucks are produced elsewhere. And that seems like a given, since Rok doesn’t build the base vehicle itself; the Hilux Champ is built in Thailand and Rok then upfits it.

Rok Trucks promises more info next year. It’s an intriguing idea, but we’ll see if it can get past the financial and regulatory headwinds necessary to bring the little pickup here at its modest price.

He can parallel-park a school bus and once drove a Lincoln Town Car 63 mph in reverse. Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • Industry observers note that waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • Industry observers note that the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Industry observers note that waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

Industry observers note that the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Sources indicate that until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

According to recent reports, most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

Industry observers note that the tech giant started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Industry observers note that everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

In a recent development, but then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

Industry observers note that the video shows two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving rapidly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation indicates that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

Sources indicate that in response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the organization to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

The DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It remarked that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

This is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

Waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

While the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Revision: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

“Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

  • It has been revealed that fiona the hippo remains under the watchful eyes of veterinarians and staff at the Cincinnati Zoo after swallowing a hat last week.
  • Last week, a knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that UPDATE, November 19, 2026, 4:15 p.m. EST: Fiona the hippo has died.

It has been revealed that fiona the hippo remains under the watchful eyes of veterinarians and staff at the Cincinnati Zoo after swallowing a hat last week. As a full-grown hippo, surgery is not an option for Fiona, but her caretakers remain hopeful she will pass the foreign object naturally.

Last week, a knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remains stuck in her digestive track. She has undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that show intestinal bunching, indicating her body is continuing to try and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests.

“Fiona ingested an object that a visitor accidentally tossed into her habitat,” the Cincinnati Zoo mentioned in a statement. “Our veterinary team and hippo care staff are monitoring her around the clock and doing everything they can to help her pass the object safely. Her care team is cautiously optimistic that she will pass it and return to her usual self. Fiona will remain off habitat until this is resolved. We will share updates as we have more information.”.

Sources indicate that the zoo also reminded patrons to be careful with their things when observing animals: “Please help us keep our animals safe by securing your belongings and taking extra care near habitats. Ingesting foreign objects can cause serious health problems for animals. If something falls into a habitat, please notify a Zoo staff member immediately.”.

On Wednesday, November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers. “The hope is that the vibrations will help encourage movement through her digestive tract and help the object pass,” the team explained.

Recent findings suggest that fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

According to recent reports, this is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has confirmed that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.
  • This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Presumably as a way of marching ever forward towards its (alleged) 100 million player goal for Battlefield 6, EA has confirmed that the multiplayer shooter will be getting its first free trial later this month.

This is, of course, specifically for players to sample the core, paid component of the game, as the recently launched Redsec remains free-to-play. Redsec, however, offers modes like battle royale and Gauntlet, which aren’t quite the traditional Battlefield experience.

Recent findings suggest that the Battlefield 6 trial arrives next Tuesday, November 25. It will run for one week, ending the following Tuesday, December 2. The trial will be available on all platforms, but won’t include all content from the full game.

In a recent development, instead, players will have access to three of the game’s maps and five of its modes. Siege of Cairo will be there alongside Season 1’s two new maps: Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields. It’s not the strongest line-up of maps, considering Eastwood is already cut from the larger Fort Lyndon battle royale map that Redsec players should be quite familiar with, but it’s something.

Recent findings suggest that as for modes, you can pick from Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch. Battlefield Studios didn’t say what the fifth mode is going to be, but a dedicated blog post with more information is set to arrive next week.

Beyond the trial's content itself, the timing is certainly great. Battlefield 6 just received one of its biggest patches, kicking off the second phase of its first season. So far this season, we’ve seen two fresh maps, several new weapons - but more importantly, solutions to problems the game’s had since launch, as well as fixes to longstanding bugs.

Industry observers note that the miserable XP progression Battlefield 6 launched with is far more tolerable. Challenges and Assignments are much easier to understand and actually finish. #29559. 5 Evidence-Based Treatments for Borderline Personality Disorder

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1051 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

5 Evidence-Based Treatments for Borderline Personality Disorder

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1051 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • It has been revealed that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat.
  • Fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 20, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

It has been revealed that for a long time, borderline personality disorder (BPD) was considered one of the most difficult mental health conditions to treat. Some therapists even believed that people with BPD couldn't get better.

Fortunately, decades of research have demonstrated otherwise. Today, several treatments can help people with BPD manage intense emotions, build healthier relationships, and reduce impulsive behaviors.

According to recent reports, dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) is probably the best known, but it's not the only option. Here are five approaches worth considering if you're looking for care for yourself or a loved one.

Developed by psychologist Marsha Linehan, DBT was the first treatment for BPD to demonstrate effectiveness in a randomized clinical trial.

Recent findings suggest that the results were incredibly promising. Among chronically suicidal women with BPD, those receiving DBT engaged in less self-harm, had fewer psychiatric hospitalizations, and were more likely to stay in treatment than those receiving usual care.

It has been revealed that since then, DBT has been evaluated in dozens of randomized clinical trials. Its strongest evidence is for reducing suicidal and self-injurious behaviors, although promising findings extend to substance use, eating disorders, and depression.

DBT is based on the idea that people with BPD experience emotions intensely and may rely on coping strategies that provide temporary relief but create problems in the long run.

Recent findings suggest that according to the treatment manual, comprehensive (full model) DBT programs include several components: weekly individual therapy, weekly skills group, and between-session phone coaching. In individual therapy, it is common to review difficulties that came up during the week and explore alternative responses. In skills group, patients receive didactic (class-like) instruction in four skill areas: mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. Between-session phone coaching helps people apply these skills when they need them most.

It has been revealed that initially, Marsha Linehan recommended that people with BPD make a year-long commitment to their DBT program. However, many DBT programs now offer care for shorter durations (e.g., 6 months).

Developed by psychologist Peter Fonagy and psychiatrist Anthony Bateman, MBT has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms, self-harm, and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

Industry observers note that MBT focuses on improving mentalizing, our ability to understand our own thoughts and feelings and those of others. Rather than explicitly teaching coping skills, as in DBT, therapists help patients strengthen this ability through interactions during therapy.

For example, imagine leaving a session convinced your therapist was annoyed with you. Rather than simply reassuring you, an MBT therapist might explore what happened and what each of you might have been thinking or feeling.

The therapeutic relationship becomes a place to practice navigating emotionally charged interactions. Treatment typically includes weekly individual and group sessions over 12–18 months.

Developed by psychiatrist Otto Kernberg and colleagues, TFP has demonstrated improvements in BPD symptoms and interpersonal functioning in randomized clinical trials.

Sources indicate that like MBT, TFP focuses on relationships rather than teaching specific coping skills. However, TFP emphasizes difficulties integrating positive and negative perceptions of ourselves and others.

For example, someone with BPD might see their partner as loving and trustworthy one moment, but cruel and uncaring after a disagreement. TFP helps patients recognize that positive and negative qualities can exist in the same person.

Treatment typically involves twice-weekly individual sessions lasting a year or longer.

Developed by psychiatrist John Gunderson, GPM takes a different approach; the goal is to make effective BPD treatment accessible through generalist mental health clinicians.

Rather than requiring extensive training in specialized psychotherapy, GPM provides a practical framework for understanding BPD, managing crises, and improving everyday functioning.

Sources indicate that particular attention is given to relationships, work, school, and other meaningful activities. Treatment typically involves weekly appointments, with flexibility based on patients' needs.

Importantly, a randomized clinical trial comparing general psychiatric management with DBT found substantial improvements in both groups, including reductions in suicidal and self-injurious behaviors.

This work challenged the assumption that effective BPD treatment necessarily requires a highly specialized, intensive program.

BPD Compass is a newer cognitive-behavioral treatment my colleagues and I developed to make evidence-based BPD care more efficient and accessible.

Industry observers note that we were intrigued that existing treatments all produce meaningful improvements, with no single approach consistently outperforming the others. This suggests that each addresses something important, whether that's emotion regulation (DBT), relationships (MBT, TFP), or building a meaningful life (GPM).

In a recent development, yet many patients continue experiencing symptoms after treatment. We wondered whether nonresponse might reflect a mismatch between patients' difficulties and the treatment they receive.

In a recent development, we designed BPD Compass to address three broad vulnerabilities associated with BPD: emotion dysregulation, relationship difficulties, and impulsivity. In our clinical trials, treatment begins with an assessment to identify which patterns are driving a particular patient's symptoms, followed by an individualized plan emphasizing the most relevant modules.

According to recent reports, BPD Compass takes 18 sessions, considerably shorter than many established BPD treatments. Like GPM, it was designed for generalist clinicians without requiring extensive specialized training.

Recent findings suggest that in an initial randomized clinical trial, participants receiving BPD Compass showed large improvements in BPD symptoms. Subsequent research also documented improvements in emotional, relational, and impulsive functioning, as well as symptoms of co-occurring conditions.

In a recent development, BPD is an incredibly heterogeneous condition. Some people experience frequent suicidal crises and need intensive, long-term support. Others may make meaningful progress with a shorter intervention.

As a BPD treatment developer, my goal isn't to replace existing treatments. It's to expand the options available. Not everyone with BPD needs year-long therapy, and we should have effective, personalized alternatives for those who don't.

Ultimately, the best treatment is one that addresses your difficulties, provides the support you need, and is accessible enough for you to receive it.

If you or someone you love is contemplating suicide, seek help immediately. For help 24/7, dial 988 for the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or reach out to the Crisis Text Line by texting TALK to 741741. To find a therapist near you, visit the Psychology Today Therapy Directory.
